newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico confirms HFCS dumping investigation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico confirms HFCS dumping investigation.

text.p: Mexico's government confirmed Thursday via its Official Gazette that it will investigate import dumping allegations of high fructose corn syrup (HFCS) and named the companies involved in the case.
Among the 17 companies listed in the investigation were grains and oilseed giant Cargill Inc, Archer Daniels Midland (ADM), CPC International and the Mexican unit of Cadbury Schweppes Plc.

Mexico's Trade Ministry announced Wednesday it is investigating a dumping suit brought forward by the Mexican Sugar Chamber, which alleges HFCS imports have entered the country at prices below cost and in "disloyal practices".

The chamber, the umbrella group for the nation's sugar industrialists, has long pushed the government to investigate their dumping charges which could result in tariffs being slapped on HFCS imports from the United States.

Corn syrup imports have slowly been gaining ground in Mexico at the expense of traditional sugars, especially in the soft drinks industry where HFCS products are easy to incorporate in production lines.
Chamber estimates put imports last year at 300,000 tonnes of class 55 HFCS, which Mexico does not produce. Experts believe corn syrup demand could rise to 1 million tonnes by the year 2000.
